system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**, described as final and agreed. | **25% / AUD 6m** cap. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The 20% fallback is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying this draft, and none is given. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping point, but only the excess above the basket is recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter to the playbook thresholds.** The draft’s thresholds and deductible basket materially narrow recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | **24 months** for general claims; separate regimes for other categories. | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** The 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits for administrative simplicity. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; insist on the separate regime.** Applying general limits to title and capacity conflicts with the playbook’s express protection. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; require the full carve-out.** These protections cannot be waived under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, in addition to specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject general deemed disclosure; retain only specific fair disclosures.** The Seller’s broad language would dilute warranties without identifying the matters fairly. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusion; if any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion.** It improperly converts access or discoverability into a defence and reaches protected categories. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. The letter says no final consent or evidence of conditions is included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Reject; make both consent and condition evidence a Completion requirement.** Delivery alone does not establish effectiveness or satisfaction of conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final security discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted; require repayment and effective releases at Completion.** The facility remains outstanding and no discharge is provided. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses excluded from the funds flow as a Seller matter; on-costs unspecified. | Specific line item or Seller-funded payment, including triggered on-costs; no silent omission from funds flow. | **Reject the omission; resolve funding and on-costs explicitly in the funds flow or Seller funding.** The disclosed conditional bonuses are not included and associated costs are unknown. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-010’s AUD 180,000 is not independent bank verification, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. | Broaden the indemnity beyond payment alone while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve the cure.** Payment, assignment and transfer of materials remain unconfirmed. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure records an unintended external email and uncertain access, scope and notification duty, with no loss amount. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantified demand in either direction. | **Do not assume either a breach or no issue; require preservation, investigation and updates.** The disclosed facts leave access, scope and consequences unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate treated as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish whether renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess the three related renewals on timing and scope; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure leaves the relevant contractual and accounting treatment unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations and remedies apply broadly to all Claims; Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories distinct, without a hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket override; preserve distinct treatment for each category.** The general language risks overriding category-specific protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence Harbourglass holds 100% of issued shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is only a supplied internal source. | **Require independent verification; do not rely on DD-012 alone.** A supplied register identifies the recorded holder but is not independent proof of title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms **open**; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Do not accept the asserted settlement; continue negotiating both categories.** The Seller’s characterization does not establish agreement or resolve the terms. |
=== END ADVICE ===
